The comparison with OxCaml was checked against typing/mode.ml (Regionality, Locality_morph, including Regional_to_local_regionality and Regional_to_global_regionality, whose right_adjoint pairing is in the same module) and typing/solver.ml (var with lower, upper and vlower).
_note_morphisms: demos-algorithms.md §3.13 says Regional_to_local/Regional_to_global go from Regionality to Locality. They do, but typing/mode.ml also has the endomorphisms Regional_to_local_regionality and Regional_to_global_regionality on Regionality, which are what the demo's regional_to_local and regional_to_global correspond to.
title: Quantifier elimination over the regionality chain
summary: The demo decides first-order formulas over the three-element chain Global < Regional < Local, the values of OxCaml's regionality axis, by quantifier elimination. `Mode_solver_public.eliminate` turns a formula into a quantifier-free one, and `eliminate_exact` proves that the two have the same truth value in every environment; projection of inequality graphs, subsumption residuals and guarded quantifier prefixes are built on it, each with an exact theorem.

This demo is not OxCaml's mode solver. Nothing in the compiler calls it, no theorem relates it to `typing/solver.ml`, it handles one axis, and it eliminates quantifiers by enumeration, so its output grows exponentially with the nesting depth of quantifiers. The [catalogue page](demo:mode-solver) states the scope.

stops.title: The interface: every operation has an exact theorem
stops.text: Each operation is declared `@@ total`, which lets the specifications apply it, and comes with an `_exact` theorem giving its result's truth value in every environment; most also have a `_scoped` theorem bounding the variables the result mentions. `eliminate_exact` is the central one: `eval_qf env (eliminate f) = eval env f` for every `env`. `decide_checked` decides a closed formula and returns `None` for one with a free variable. `regionality_adjunction` is a fact about the chain: `regional_to_local` is left adjoint to `regional_to_global`.

stops.title: The specification: evaluation over three values
stops.text: Terms are constants, de Bruijn variables, join, meet, `Regional_to_global` and arbitrary lookup tables from the chain to itself; the tables need not be monotone, so terms are more general than mode morphisms. Atoms are `≤` between terms. `eval` reads `Exists a` as the disjunction of `a` with `Global`, `Regional` and `Local` pushed on the environment, and `Forall a` as the conjunction. An unbound variable evaluates to `Global`.

stops.title: A client
stops.from: let (residual_value @ total) env gamma guard obligation :
stops.text: The client uses only the public interface and the three semantics modules. Each function returns a `bool` refined to equal the truth value of a formula from the semantics, and its proof is one erased call to the matching `_exact` theorem. The assertions run as native code: with `equality` saying that the two innermost variables are equal, `∀∃ equality` holds and `∃∀ equality` does not, a formula with a free variable gives `None`, and the guarded game with prefix `[Universal; Existential]` is won while the reversed one is lost.

stops.title: The public module hides the definitions
stops.text: The public module defines each operation from the proof modules: `eliminate` is `Mode_solver_three_qe_proof.eliminate`, and `eliminate_exact` unfolds it once and applies the proof module's theorem. The definition is `[@def]` here, but the interface declares only `val eliminate : formula -> qf`, so its equation lemma is not exported and a client knows the result only through the theorems. The demo has no rejection test: nothing checks that a false claim about these operations fails to check.

stops.title: Guarded prefixes read as a game
stops.to: admissible prefix env guard && game prefix env guard witness
stops.text: `admissible prefix env guard` says that some values of the prefix's variables satisfy `guard`. `game` reads the prefix as a two-player game in which each move must leave `guard` satisfiable for the rest of the prefix: the existential player must find such a value, the universal player ranges over such values only, and at the end the values must satisfy `witness`. `normalized_game` conjoins the two, and `project_admissible_exact` states that `project_admissible` computes it. Like `eval`, these are ordinary total functions that enumerate the chain.

stops.title: The algorithm: elimination by enumeration
to: And (subst_qf Regional q, subst_qf Local q))
stops.text: `subst_term` replaces variable 0 by a constant and shifts the other variables down. `eliminate` works bottom-up: a quantifier over an already eliminated body becomes three copies of it, with the bound variable replaced by each value of the chain, joined by `Or` for `Exists` and `And` for `Forall`. Nothing simplifies the result, so its size grows as 3 to the power of the quantifier nesting depth, and no running time is stated.

stops.title: The core proof
stops.text: `eliminate_exact` is structural induction on the formula. For a quantifier it applies the induction hypothesis in each of the three extended environments and the substitution lemma `subst_qf_exact`, `eval_qf env (subst_qf v q) = eval_qf (v :: env) q`, proved above through `subst_term_exact` and `lookup_shift`. The `_def` calls unfold `eliminate`, `eval` and `eval_qf` one level each, since the checker does not unfold definitions on its own. The demo trusts nothing beyond the shared base: the checker, Z3 and the compiler.

stops.title: Everything else reduces to eliminate
stops.from: let[@def] rec (project @ total) prefix guard witness =
stops.text: Guarded projection walks the prefix from the inside out, keeping two quantifier-free formulas: `domain` (the guard is satisfiable) and `winning`. At each quantifier it eliminates `∃x. domain`, and either `∃x. domain ∧ winning` or `∀x. ¬domain ∨ winning`. Graph projection in [`mode_solver_graph_qe_proof.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/mode_solver_graph_qe_proof.ml) compiles the inequalities to a conjunction and eliminates the existential quantifiers over it. `project_scopes_compose` proves that projecting a prefix in two parts gives the same formulas, as syntax trees, as projecting it at once.

stops.title: What OxCaml has instead
stops.to: (** Maps regional to global, identity otherwise. *)
stops.text: OxCaml's regionality axis is the same chain, and its morphisms include `Regional_to_local_regionality` and `Regional_to_global_regionality`, the adjoint pair that `regionality_adjunction` states. The mode solver in [`typing/solver.ml`](src:typing/solver.ml) works differently: it keeps mutable variables with lower and upper bounds and morphism edges (`vlower`), and propagates constraints incrementally over products of axes. The demo is not that solver. Nothing in the compiler calls the demo, and no theorem relates the two; it is a verified reference procedure for one axis.
